event: The last thing you remember is your reading chair, a book and a lamp, the house quiet.
A deep booming voice speaks inside your head, in no language you know, and you look up.

memory.fact: A deep booming voice in no tongue Alan knew spoke inside his head, and then the chair was gone.
A deep booming voice in no tongue Alan knew spoke inside his head, and then the chair was gone.

event: It comes again, harder, pressing on the inside of your skull, and the chair is gone.
Black nothing with no stars: the air rips out of your mouth, ears spike, eyes sting.

memory.fact: The last thing Alan remembers is his reading chair, then a black airless nothing.
The last thing Alan remembers is his reading chair, then a black airless nothing.

event: Then light, a hard soft landing on your back, and air.

memory.fact: Nala landed in Fern Hollow in the late afternoon of day one.

event: You lie and breathe in ragged gulps of cool, wet, green-smelling air; your chest hurts.
The ringing fades: water trickling, leaves high up, a ticking in the undergrowth like a clock.

memory.fact: Something unseen in the hollow's ferns ticks and clicks like a clock with too many hands.
Something unseen in the hollow's ferns ticks and clicks like a clock with too many hands.

event: You open your eyes on enormous straight trees, grey-scaled bark, blue-green leaves, gold light.

memory.fact: The hollow's trees are huge and straight, with bark like grey scales and bluish leaves.
The hollow's trees are huge and straight, with bark like grey scales and bluish leaves.

event: You lie in deep springy moss, in a round hollow full of ferns taller than you sitting.

memory.fact: Fern Hollow is a bowl-shaped clearing in an old forest, floored with moss and ferns.
Fern Hollow is a bowl-shaped clearing in an old forest, floored with moss and ferns.

event: You sit up and everything is wrong: your weight sits differently, your arms are too short.
Your dark grey shirt hangs loose to mid-thigh, its collar slipping off one shoulder.

memory.fact: She wears Alan's loose dark grey shirt, which hangs to her mid-thigh and gapes at the collar.
She wears Alan's loose dark grey shirt, which hangs to her mid-thigh and gapes at the collar.

event: Your black compression tights are snug as ever; you have no shoes.

memory.fact: She wears Alan's black compression tights, which still fit her snugly.
She wears Alan's black compression tights, which still fit her snugly.

event: Your feet and hands are small, pale, narrow and freckled.
A heavy fall of dark red hair slides forward over your shoulder.

memory.fact: Her hair is long, heavy and dark red, falling past her shoulder blades.
Her hair is long, heavy and dark red, falling past her shoulder blades.

event: You say something, and the voice that says it is a woman's.

memory.fact: Alan landed in a woman's body.
Alan landed in a woman's body.

event: A blue box flashes before your eyes, turns with your head, and is understood as you read.

memory.fact: Davrar's blue boxes hang before the eyes, turn with the head, and are understood as they are read.
Davrar's blue boxes hang before the eyes, turn with the head, and are understood as they are read.
Davrar's boxes are blue and appear front and center in the eyes.
A box is understood as if pulled from memory, before it is fully read.

event: "Welcome to Davrar. Davrar will help you survive."

memory.fact: A blue box welcomed Nala to Davrar and said Davrar would help her survive.
A blue box welcomed Nala to Davrar and said Davrar would help her survive.

event: The clicking in the ferns has stopped.
A spring wells up between two roots on the low side and runs downhill as a clear brook.

memory.fact: A spring wells up between two roots on the hollow's low side and runs downhill as a clear brook.
A spring wells up between two roots on the hollow's low side and runs downhill as a clear brook.
A spring rises in the hollow's low side and runs off as a clear, cold brook.

event: Far off, something whistles three rising notes, and something else answers.
In the deepening shade, faint green lights begin to drift as the light goes golden.

memory.fact: Faint green lights drift under the canopy over the hollow as the light goes golden toward dusk.
Faint green lights drift under the canopy over the hollow as the light goes golden toward dusk.

event: "Okay... isekai protocol," you say, in the new voice, clear and a little hoarse.

memory.fact: Her voice is a woman's, clear and a little hoarse.
Her voice is a woman's, clear and a little hoarse.

event: "System?" "Status?" "Davrar?" Each time the air in front of you stays empty.

memory.fact: Until Davrar finishes integrating her, asking for status brings no box.

event: The name Davrar snags on a half-memory from somewhere else: "I remember that name."
You ask Nathan, if he has merged with the system, to send you help.
No answer comes: no voice, no blue light; your own voice was the only human sound.

memory.fact: Davrar shows boxes and never converses; words said to it get no answer.

event: The clickers stay quiet a long while, then one starts up, another answers, and all resume.

memory.fact: The ticking in the hollow's ferns falls quiet at a voice, then starts up again after a while.
The ticking in the hollow's ferns falls quiet at a voice, then starts up again after a while.

event: Minutes go by; the light slants lower, and the cooling air reaches your bare feet first.
Far off, the three rising notes come again, and the answer comes back.

memory.fact: Three rising whistled notes sound far off around the hollow toward dusk, and are answered.
Three rising whistled notes sound far off around the hollow toward dusk, and are answered.

event: More green lights drift down; one brushes a fern by your knee, and its edge glows and fades.

memory.fact: Faint green lights drift under the canopy at dusk, and the ferns glow where they touch.

event: Beyond the hollow's rim, the shade between the trunks has gone blue-grey.
You are barefoot, with nothing in your hands, beside the spring and its brook.

memory.fact: She has no shoes, no money and nothing in her hands.
She has no shoes, no money and nothing in her hands.

event: No help yet, you think, but if you survive, you get something.
You plan a spiral search out from the spring, eyes open for danger, hoping for an inspect skill.
You get up and circle outward from the water, slowly, ring by ring.
The brook bed is smooth rounded grey stones, the water cold enough to ache.
Dead branches lie everywhere; those hung up off the ground snap dry in your hands.

memory.fact: Dead branches lie everywhere under the trees; the ones off the ground are dry.
Dead branches lie everywhere under the trees; the ones off the ground are dry.

event: The moss is littered with shed grey bark scales, each hand-sized and hard as horn.

memory.fact: Scalebark bark is overlapping grey scales, each hand-sized and hard as horn.
Scalebark bark is overlapping grey scales, each hand-sized and hard as horn.

event: A scale's edge opens a thin red line in your fingertip; you suck it and go more carefully.

memory.fact: Shed bark scales are hand-sized, hard as horn, with edges sharp enough to cut cord or skin.
Shed bark scales are hand-sized, hard as horn, with edges sharp enough to cut cord or skin.
Shed scalebark scales have edges sharp enough to cut cord or skin.
Shed scalebark scales have edges sharp enough to cut cord or skin.

event: Forty yards east of the spring lies a fallen giant, its root end hollow, dry and crawlable.

memory.fact: Forty yards east of the spring lies a fallen scalebark, its root end hollow, dry and crawlable.
Forty yards east of the spring lies a fallen scalebark, its root end hollow, dry and crawlable.

event: You pull at its core: soft dry punk full of fibre that crumbles to shreds.

memory.fact: The fallen trunk's rotted core is soft, dry punk full of fibre that crumbles to shreds.
The fallen trunk's rotted core is soft, dry punk full of fibre that crumbles to shreds.

event: Sixty yards down the brook, tall canes crowd the bank, hung with ripe dark-red berries.

memory.fact: Brookberry canes line the brook sixty yards below the spring, hung with ripe dark-red berries.
Brookberry canes line the brook sixty yards below the spring, hung with ripe dark-red berries.

event: In the hollow's shade grow low bushes of sweet-smelling blue-black berries; you eat neither.

memory.fact: Low bushes in the hollow's shade bear sweet-smelling blue-black berries.
Low bushes in the hollow's shade bear sweet-smelling blue-black berries.

event: Eighty yards down the brook, a cut bank shows a seam of dark glassy stone like flint.

memory.fact: The brook bed is rounded grey stones; eighty yards down, a bank shows dark glassy flint.
The brook bed is rounded grey stones; eighty yards down, a bank shows dark glassy flint.

event: On the south rim, a low trail through the ferns, with pellet droppings and nibbled fern tips.

memory.fact: A small trail through ferns on the hollow's south rim is marked by pellets and nibbled fern.
A small trail through ferns on the hollow's south rim is marked by pellets and nibbled fern.

event: The canopy closes everywhere; from nowhere in the hollow can you see past it.

memory.fact: The canopy closes over the hollow; no view of the land beyond can be had from it.
The canopy closes over the hollow; no view of the land beyond can be had from it.

event: The last of the light goes grey as you work along the upslope rim.
A trunk there is scored with deep claw marks, the bark scales shredded, the highest at head height.

memory.fact: On the upslope rim, a trunk is scored by deep claw marks at head height, the bark shredded.
On the upslope rim, a trunk is scored by deep claw marks at head height, the bark shredded.

event: It smells of musk, and scat full of grey fur and bone lies near its roots.

memory.fact: The clawed trunk smells of musk, and scat with grey fur and bone bits lies near its roots.
The clawed trunk smells of musk, and scat with grey fur and bone bits lies near its roots.

event: You stay crouched there, studying the marks, while the last light goes.
Full dark: black under the canopy, but for green specks and the ticking, patchy now.
A heavy grey shape bursts out behind you, swerves off a stride short with a hiss, and is gone.

memory.fact: A heavy grey beast burst from the ferns at Nala at full dark, day one, and swerved off hissing.
A heavy grey beast burst from the ferns at Nala at full dark, day one, and swerved off hissing.

event: You turn from the clawed trunk and start quietly back toward the log, meaning to hide inside.
The log's mouth is eighty yards off, down the slope and across the hollow, and you can't see it.

memory.fact: The fallen log's mouth lies eighty yards downslope of the clawed trunk, across the hollow.
The fallen log's mouth lies eighty yards downslope of the clawed trunk, across the hollow.

event: You go by feel: waist-high ferns, moss, roots, a bark scale under your heel.

memory.fact: Between them is a fern slope, waist-high, over moss, roots and scattered bark scales.
Between them is a fern slope, waist-high, over moss, roots and scattered bark scales.

event: You set each bare foot down slowly and keep your breath slow and shallow.
The green specks light nothing; they are only points to steer between.

memory.fact: In full dark the drifting green lights light nothing; they are only points to steer between.
In full dark the drifting green lights light nothing; they are only points to steer between.

event: Your mouth is dry; you have drunk nothing since you landed.
The ferns fall quiet right at your feet as you pass, and start up again behind you.

memory.fact: The ferns' ticking falls quiet right around anyone walking through, then resumes behind them.
The ferns' ticking falls quiet right around anyone walking through, then resumes behind them.

event: About halfway to the log, the ticking behind you stops in a patch.
The patch of quiet slides along behind you, low in the ferns, closing faster than you walk.

memory.fact: Night, day one: something large moved under the ferns toward Nala's back as she crept to the log.
Night, day one: something large moved under the ferns toward Nala's back as she crept to the log.
Before the strike, the ferns' ticking hushes in a patch closing in behind the prey.

event: Something large is moving under the ferns toward you; the log's mouth is still forty yards off.
You run, straight for the log through the ferns, blind.
A root jars your heel and a bark scale bites the ball of your foot, and you keep going.

memory.fact: Shed bark scales on the ground are hard-edged and nick bare feet that drag or slip.

event: Behind you something tears through the ferns, gaining so fast its sound seems to jump at you.

memory.fact: Prey that breaks into a run draws the gloamcat's rush at once; it runs far faster than a person.

event: Ten yards short of the log's mouth, a heavy weight hits you from behind, high and low at once.

memory.fact: Rushing Nala as she runs for the log, it reaches her back ten yards short of the log's mouth.
Rushing Nala as she runs for the log, it reaches her back ten yards short of the log's mouth.
Its rush from behind ends in a leap for the back of the neck, heavy and low.

event: Teeth close on the back of your neck and shoulder, and you go down face first into the ferns.
The pain is huge and hot, then a single point; blood runs warm down under your shirt.

changes.note: The beast's first bite, at the back of Nala's neck and shoulder, takes eight health

event: It does not let go: hot breath on your skin, its weight pinning your back, a growl in your bones.
You claw forward, elbows and knees, dragging it with you toward the log's mouth.
Your fingers find the torn edge of the roots, and you haul your head and shoulders into the gap.

memory.fact: The fallen log's hollow is dry and close inside, and smells of rot and earth.
The fallen log's hollow is dry and close inside, and smells of rot and earth.

event: The jaws open, and close again, harder and deeper, on the back of your neck and shoulder.

changes.note: The second, deeper bite takes seven more, leaving Nala grievous at five

memory.fact: Night, day one: the beast bit the back of Nala's neck and shoulder twice as she crawled for the log.
Night, day one: the beast bit the back of Nala's neck and shoulder twice as she crawled for the log.

event: Your arms shake and the edges of your sight go grey, half in the log, your legs still outside.
Its jaws shift on your neck, and its weight settles on your back for another bite.
You twist, meaning to catch its jaws, get your legs round its neck and choke it.
The roots hem your shoulders and its weight pins your hips; you wrench half round anyway.
One hand finds coarse thick fur, a cheek hard as bone, a hot wet lip and teeth behind it.

memory.fact: The beast's fur is coarse and thick, and its cheek under the fur is hard as bone.
The beast's fur is coarse and thick, and its cheek under the fur is hard as bone.

event: You grip, but your fingers have no strength left in them, and they slide off.

memory.fact: Night, day one: in the log's mouth, Nala's fingers had no strength left to grip the beast's jaws.
Night, day one: in the log's mouth, Nala's fingers had no strength left to grip the beast's jaws.

event: Your legs are still out in the ferns under its weight, and you can't get them free.
The jaws open, and close a third time, deep in the side of your neck.

changes.note: The third bite, deep in the side of the neck, takes her last five and she goes down

memory.fact: Night, day one: the beast bit Nala a third time, deep in the side of her neck.
Night, day one: the beast bit Nala a third time, deep in the side of her neck.

event: The pain goes far away; the dark of the log goes darker, then there is nothing.
Unfelt, it drags you by the neck out of the log's mouth and up the slope into the thick ferns.

memory.fact: Prey that goes limp it drags away by the neck to eat.
Night, day one: it drags Nala out of the log's mouth and twenty yards upslope into thick fern.

event: You don't wake. You die there, in the ferns above the hollow, on your first night in Davrar.

memory.fact: Nala dies of her wounds in the ferns about 19:10 on day one, without waking.
Nothing in the wood or beyond it comes to Nala's aid on the night of day one.
